snippet.textDisplay: Bless you gorgeous lady! I also take care of my sick Mother who is in the first stage of Dementia. I work 40 plus hours as a nurse, but every day my shift doesn’t begin until I get home. At work, I have help, but at home I have none, period. There are days that I think I can’t take another step, but some days are joyful. Those who have been blessed enough to not know our struggles have no idea how mentally it drains you. I’m not complaining and I would do it all over again for my precious Mom. The fact is, when you take care of a parent or anyone with this disease, your life completely stops and your whole attention is on that loved one and giving them the best care possible. Thankfully, I still have my Mom at home and we do the best we can do. Crystal, you absolutely put your precious mother upon a pedestal where she belongs by being there every single day. You do it with grace and dignity. I respect you my sister! Your mom is well taken care of and I’m glad you are able to live your life as well! Keep being gorgeous! Sending love from TN.🧡

snippet.textDisplay:
You are right about one minute from the next! I work in the feild at assisted living and I work with patients/ residents from every stand point and dementia units are bitter sweet. Ive got it all to happen to me believe that. From swatting, slapping, kicking, punching, spitting, you name it. Its happened to me. What's hard about it for me specifically is i have my days where I cant afford another lick but I get em anyway regardless of what im going through in my life. Its a very high stress level job. And you do not get paid well from these companies. At all. But when you're in it because its your passion and you were called you have to understand God sent you there, you're on an assignment and You will be rewarded for God's work because that what it is. I have my days I want to burst into tears and just walk away trust me but I pray to god for strength 💪 to keep going! Because its like that. The thing right now is though im caring for other people's family but my mom and grandparents I haven't had to experience this yet with my own and I think thats 100xs harder to see your own mom not remember anything when they were once the person you went to for everything 💔 I couldn't imagine 💔 just seeing my mom like this but... ill never give in or up on my mom and id definitely give her all the love and care I could. I do recommend cameras in your loved ones rooms. When family is there ir watching alot of staff put on but out of sight ive seen some real hateful rude mean staff that are not and should not be around vulnerable people. However these places cant keep enough staff to be that choosy. They take in anyone who they can get in it for the work and the pay
Alot of people dont and cant do personal care and its alot 💯 just one hour can drain a worker. Im telling you this because ive been doing it so long. I feel beat up mentally and physically. But I know they depend on me and god is dependent on me to fulfill assignments he has made for me. Its definitely a full time slash overtime job and it never ends. Ive seen it all! Another thing its expensive! For these people to be able to stay at an AL facility. My goodness 😳 its unbelievable and nursing homes are even more expensive. 😢 crystal 🔮 u have my heart ❤️ all.the way outta SC baby. I mean that darlin. I do. I'm so happy to see you loving her taking her out getting her out to do things 💗 alot of family members ik dont have the time or patience or mental state to do what you do and I thank u ❤ from the heart

snippet.textDisplay:
100% correct!!! Thank you for sharing your journey with your mom with dementia!!! My story is exactly the same!! It’s hard work and anyone who has walked in our shoes will understand!! Like you I did not want to put my mom into a facility but the threats to my family from my mom were getting to real for us. It broke my heart to place my mom in a memory care. Let me tell ALL YOU PEOPLE WHO JUDGE!!! You do what’s good for your wellbeing but for me I was able to enjoy being with my mom better in a facility rather than at my home. With all the stress caring and trying to keep my mom safe 24/7 and her multiple mood swings/triggers. It’s hard to enjoy your loved one. In the facility I got to enjoy being and visiting with her. Now saying all this you can’t just throw your loved one into a facility and forget about them you have to be involved with the facility and your loved one. Do the activities with your love one such as crafts, games, picnics, dances and other activities. You won’t be disappointed and you both will have fun ❤❤❤
Thank you again for sharing your journey. My mom has passed away 1.5 years and your beautiful mom reminds me so much of my mom. Stay strong beautiful ladies ❤❤❤
